newsitem.title: USA: St. Jude Medical to proceed with Ventritex merger.
newsitem.headline: St. Jude Medical to proceed with Ventritex merger.

text.p: St. Jude Medical Corp said Thursday that, based on information available about reported failures of a component of a Ventritex Inc product, it is proceeding with a proposed merger with the California-based medical devices firm.
"We are proceeding with the merger. We still anticipate the transaction will be completed by the end of this quarter," the company said in a statement.
St. Jude declined comment on the product. "It is not appropriate for St. Jude Medical to comment on the specifics of this product situation," the statement said.

Ventritex management has kept St. Jude informed of its analysis of a small number of reported failures of a component in its Cadence implanted defibrillator, it said, including discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on the necessary software modifications to deal with this situation.

"We believe Ventritex has acted responsibly and in a proactive manner to analyze these product failures, communicate with the FDA, and inform their physician customers on the appropriate modifications to deal with this component problem," St. Jude said.

Earlier today, Ventritex said it will reprogram two defibrillators models in response to the recent failure of an electrical component in two implanted Cadence defibrillators which resulted in a the delivery of inappropriately rapid pacing pulses. The company said the rapid pacing is believed to have been associated with the death of two patients.

St. Jude said it continues to work with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to receive the necessary clearances to complete the merger of Ventritex into St. Jude Medical, as announced on October 23, 1996.
St. Jude develops, makes and distributes medical devices for the worldwide cardiovascular market.
Shares of St. Jude were trading off 1/8 to 36-7/8. Shares of Ventritex were trading off three to 17-7/8.
